newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mostly down on exports, spreads.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mostly down on exports, spreads.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended mostly lower on Thursday, led by old crop contracts on mediocre USDA export sales and unwinding of bull spreads, traders said.

"Today was a reaction to disappointing export sales," said Mario Balletto, oilseeds analyst with Merrill Lynch. "That set the tone. I think we have priced buyers out of the market. The question is, have we priced them out enough?"
USDA Thursday said U.S. net soybean export sales in the week ended March 27 totaled 216,400 tonnes, below expectations for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes and 44 percent below last week.
"We saw some profit taking on the spreads," Balletto added. "They've had a big move over the last couple of weeks or so."
The July/November spread narrowed 13 cents per bushel and closed at $1.73-3/4, premium July. On March 5, the spread closed at $1.00 per bushel, premium July.
Uncertainty about the magnitude of a port strike in Brazil further pressured nearbys. Stevedores at Paranagua port had not yet decided whether to join calls for a national strike.
Soybeans ended 12-1/2 cents per bushel lower to three cents higher with May down 12-1/2 at $8.71.
Selling of cash soybeans were reported before the market opened and commercial hedge selling was noted.

"There was a little selling this morning," said Doug Hjort, president of Hjort Associates in Iowa. "There's going to be very little selling now on lower money. They'll just close the bin door, plant the new crop and come back in June and take a look at it (stocks)."
On the day, ADM sold two million bushels May while Cargill Inc sold one million May and two million July, traders said.
Funds sold at least 10 million bushels. CIS sold three million May and Smith Barney sold 2.5 million May, two million July, one million August and 3.5 million September.

Continental Grain spread 1.5 million November/July at 18-1/2, premium July, Tenco Inc spread 2.3 million November/July at $1.80 to $1.79 and Iowa Grain spread 1.2 million at $1.80-1/2 to $1.79, traders said.

In options, Continental bought 650 July $9.00 calls and sold 650 July $10.00 calls at 21-1/2 cents. Continental also bought 400 July $8.75 puts and sold 400 July $7.75 puts at 38-1/2 cents, floor sources said.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 65,000 contracts, compared with 75,916 contracts on Wednesday.
